name: Account Opening Process
description: The formal end-to-end procedure for opening new bank accounts at FirstUK Bank. Managed by the Head of Retail Banking and applicable to Branch Staff, Customer Service, Operations, and Compliance teams.

name: Head of Retail Banking
description: The designated owner of the Account Opening SOP, responsible for the oversight and governance of the retail banking account opening procedures.

name: Branch Staff
description: Personnel located within bank branches who are part of the target audience and executors of the account opening procedure.
context: Audience | Branch Staff, Customer Service, Operations, Compliance

name: Customer Service
description: Staff members providing customer support services who are required to adhere to the account opening SOP.
context: Audience | Branch Staff, Customer Service, Operations, Compliance

name: Operations
description: The operational department responsible for the back-end processing and execution of account opening tasks.
context: Audience | Branch Staff, Customer Service, Operations, Compliance

name: Compliance
description: The compliance team responsible for ensuring the account opening process meets regulatory requirements and internal policies.
context: Audience | Branch Staff, Customer Service, Operations, Compliance

name: Customer Account Opening Process
description: A standardized operational workflow for opening SmartSaver, Current, and Mortgage accounts. The process is executed across branch, online, and postal channels to ensure regulatory compliance, data accuracy, and consistent customer experience.
context: Establish standardized procedures for opening customer accounts (SmartSaver, Current, Mortgage)
across all channels (branch, online, postal) to ensure regulatory compliance, data accuracy, and consistent customer experience.

name: SmartSaver Account
description: A specific banking product available for opening under the standardized customer account opening procedures.

name: Current Account
description: A specific banking product available for opening under the standardized customer account opening procedures.

name: Mortgage Account
description: A specific banking product available for opening under the standardized customer account opening procedures.

name: New Customer Account Opening Process
description: The end-to-end operational procedure for opening accounts for new customers. This process covers all banking product types, including savings, current accounts, and mortgages, and is applicable across branch, online, and postal channels.
context: Applies to: New customer account openings

name: Savings Account
description: A type of banking product governed by the New Customer Account Opening Process.

name: Current Account
description: A type of banking product governed by the New Customer Account Opening Process.

name: Mortgage Product
description: A type of banking product governed by the New Customer Account Opening Process.

name: Head Office Staff
description: Personnel located at the head office responsible for executing account opening procedures.

name: Branch Staff
description: Personnel located at bank branches responsible for executing account opening procedures.

name: Account Opening Process
description: The end-to-end operational workflow for establishing a new customer account. The timeline varies by channel: 1–2 business days for online/branch and 5–7 days for postal applications.

name: Customer Request
description: The initial stage of the account opening process where the customer expresses intent to open an account.

name: Channel Selection
description: The step where the method of application is determined, specifically whether it is processed via Branch, Online, or Postal channels.

name: Application Form Completion
description: The stage where the necessary application forms are filled out by the customer.

name: KYC Verification
description: A step involving the verification of the customer's identity and address documents.

name: AML Screening
description: The process of screening the applicant against Anti-Money Laundering lists and criteria.

name: Risk Assessment
description: The evaluation of the customer's risk profile to determine the suitability of opening the account.

name: Approval or Rejection Decision
description: A critical branching point where the application is either approved for account creation or rejected based on the preceding verification and risk steps.

name: Account Creation
description: The action of establishing the account in the bank's systems, contingent upon the approval decision.

name: Card Issuance
description: The step where a payment card is issued to the customer, if applicable to the chosen product.

name: Customer Notification
description: The stage where the customer is informed of the outcome of their application and the status of their account.

name: Account Activation
description: The final step to make the newly created account operational for the customer.

name: Customer
description: The individual applying for a new account who initiates the request and completes the application form.

name: Account Opening Process
description: The end-to-end procedure for opening a bank account, initiated by a customer's request at a branch. It involves product selection and initial greeting, with an estimated time of 5 minutes for the first stage.

name: Customer Intent Identification
description: The initial interaction where the customer explicitly states their intention to open a savings account.
context: Customer states intent: "I want to open a savings account"

name: Customer Greeting and Seating
description: The staff member welcomes the customer and provides a designated seating area to begin the process.
context: Branch staff greets customer, offers seating

name: Account Opening Form Retrieval
description: The process of accessing the necessary account opening documentation, which can be provided in either paper or tablet format.
context: Branch staff pulls up account opening form (paper or tablet)

name: Product Availability Explanation
description: Staff provides an overview of the available banking products, including SmartSaver and Current Accounts.
context: Explain products available (SmartSaver, Current Account, etc.)

name: Branch Staff
description: The employee responsible for greeting the customer, retrieving opening forms, and explaining product options.
context: Branch staff greets customer, offers seating
Branch staff pulls up account opening form

name: Customer
description: The individual visiting the branch to initiate the account opening process and select a banking product.

name: Product Selection Gate
description: A branching point where the customer selects the specific product they wish to open, leading to different account types: SmartSaver, Current Account, or Mortgage.

name: SmartSaver Account
description: A savings-specific banking product available for selection during the account opening process.

name: Current Account
description: A transactional banking product available for selection during the account opening process.

name: Mortgage
description: A lending-based product available for selection during the account opening process.

name: Online Account Opening Process
description: The end-to-end digital workflow for customers to open a bank account via the website. The process takes approximately 15–20 minutes if documentation is ready.

name: Customer
description: The individual initiating the account opening process by interacting with the bank's website and providing necessary information and documentation.

name: Website Navigation to Open Account Page
description: The initial action where the customer accesses the specific 'Open Account' landing page on the bank's website.

name: Product Type Selection
description: The step where the customer chooses the specific banking product they wish to open.

name: Online Form Completion
description: The stage where the customer fills out the required digital application forms.

name: KYC Verification Execution
description: The phase of the online application where the customer undergoes identity and address verification procedures.

name: KYC Compliance Gate
description: A mandatory regulatory check within the online opening process to verify customer identity before the account can be opened.

name: Postal Account Opening Process
description: An end-to-end workflow for opening a bank account via mail. It involves request, mailing of forms, customer completion, and backend processing with an estimated timeline of 5–7 days.

name: Postal Pack Request
description: The initial stage where a customer requests a postal application pack through phone support or the bank's website.
context: Phone support or website requests postal pack

name: Application Form Dispatch
description: The action of mailing application forms to the customer, which includes providing a prepaid envelope for return.
context: Application forms mailed to customer (with prepaid envelope)

name: Application Completion and Return
description: The stage where the customer fills out the provided application forms and returns them to the bank via mail.
context: Customer completes and returns by mail

name: Application Processing
description: The final stage where the returned application is processed by the internal operations staff.

name: Customer
description: The individual requesting the account opening and responsible for completing and returning the postal application forms.
context: Customer completes and returns by mail

name: Phone Support
description: The channel or staff responsible for receiving postal pack requests via telephone.
context: Phone support or website requests postal pack

name: Website
description: The digital interface used by customers to request a postal application pack.
context: Phone support or website requests postal pack

name: Operations Team
description: The internal bank team responsible for processing the completed application forms received by mail.

name: Application Form Completion
description: The second stage of the onboarding process where the applicant's personal details, financial information, and product preferences are collected. This step ensures all necessary data for account opening and compliance is captured.

name: Applicant
description: The individual applying for a banking product, whose personal and financial details are collected during the Application Form Completion step.

name: Customer Address Collection
description: The process of capturing the applicant's current address and any previous addresses if they have lived at their current residence for less than 3 years.

name: Product Selection
description: The selection of the specific banking product type and associated features requested by the applicant.

name: Card Type Selection
description: The identification of the specific payment card type the applicant wishes to receive as part of their product selection.

name: Standing Order Setup Identification
description: The identification of any known standing orders the customer intends to set up during the application process.

name: Direct Debit Setup Identification
description: The identification of any known direct debit mandates the customer intends to establish during the application process.

name: New Account Setup
description: The target account being established through the collection of personal and financial data, including access preferences.

name: Data Accuracy Checks Process
description: The operational workflow used to ensure that customer information is accurate, complete, and correctly formatted across different application channels including Branch, Online, and Postal.

name: Branch Staff
description: Personnel responsible for verifying customer information, spelling, and contact details during in-person interactions.

name: Customer Information Verification
description: A step performed by Branch Staff to confirm the accuracy of provided information directly with the customer.

name: Spelling and Accuracy Review
description: A review step conducted by Branch Staff to ensure all entered data is spelled correctly and accurate.

name: Contact Details Confirmation
description: A verification step where Branch Staff confirm that the customer's contact information is correct.

name: Completeness Review
description: A final check performed by Branch Staff to ensure no required information is missing from the application.

name: Online Validation System
description: The automated system responsible for real-time validation of data formats and mandatory field presence for online applications.

name: Real-time Field Validation
description: Automated check of data formats, such as email and postcode, performed instantly during the online application process.

name: Mandatory Field Check
description: An automated check to ensure all required fields are populated before an online application can be submitted.

name: Online Address Postcode Verification
description: Automated verification of the customer's postcode during the online submission process.

name: Operations Staff
description: Personnel responsible for reviewing postal applications for completeness and clarity of handwriting.

name: Postal Completeness Review
description: A manual review conducted by Operations staff to ensure postal applications are complete.

name: Missing Information Customer Outreach
description: A step where Operations staff contact the customer to obtain information that was missing from a postal application.

name: Handwriting Verification
description: A review process where Operations staff verify unclear handwriting on postal documents to ensure data accuracy.

name: Identity Verification (KYC)
description: A discrete operational step focused on verifying the identity of the customer. This step refers to a separate detailed policy document for the full KYC procedures.

name: Account Opening Process
description: The end-to-end procedure for opening a bank account, encompassing three distinct channels: Branch, Online, and Postal. The process defines the specific documentation and certification requirements based on the chosen channel.

name: Branch Document Examination
description: The step in the account opening process where physical, original identification documents are examined at a branch location.

name: Online Document Submission
description: The stage where customers provide digital scans or photos of their identification documents for account opening via the online channel.
context: Scan/photo of passport or driving license

name: Postal Document Submission
description: The stage where customers submit a scan attached to an application along with notarized copies via post.
context: Notarized copy (certified by solicitor, notary, etc.)

name: UK Passport
description: An acceptable form of primary identification used across Branch, Online, and Postal opening channels.
context: Scan/photo of passport or driving license

name: UK Driving License
description: An acceptable form of identification, specifically requiring a photocard format for branch openings.
context: Scan/photo of passport or driving license

name: Notary or Solicitor
description: An external authorized professional responsible for certifying the authenticity of document copies for Online and Postal account openings.
context: Notarized copy (certified by solicitor, notary, etc.)

name: Verification Process
description: An operational workflow for verifying customer identity documents through three distinct channels: Branch, Online, and Postal. Processing times vary by channel from under 1 minute (Online) to 2 business days (Postal).

name: Document Collection Step
description: The initial stage of the verification process involving requesting a primary identity document, recording its details (number, issue/expiry dates), and ensuring the document has not expired.

name: Physical Verification Step
description: A branch-specific verification action where the staff examines the document, compares the photo to the customer, validates the signature, and notes any concerns.

name: System Recording Step
description: The final stage of the process where the document type and number are entered into the AMS system, linked to the customer record, and marked as verified.

name: Branch Staff
description: The personnel responsible for executing the Physical Verification step and managing the branch processing timeline of 10 minutes.

name: AMS System
description: The system of record used to link document details to the customer record and track the verification status.

name: Document Validity Check
description: A check to determine if the identity document is valid or has expired, which is a prerequisite for completing Step 1.

name: Customer
description: The individual whose identity is being verified and whose appearance is compared against the provided identity document.

name: Primary Identity Document
description: The official document collected from the customer, consisting of a photo, signature, and issue/expiry dates.

name: Address Verification Step
description: A discrete action within the operational workflow focused on verifying the customer's address. Detailed procedures for this step are governed by the customer identification policy.
context: See [[policy_customer_identification]] for detailed address verification procedures.

name: Customer Identification Process
description: The overarching policy and procedural framework governing how FirstUK Bank identifies customers and verifies their address details.
context: See [[policy_customer_identification]] for detailed address verification procedures.

name: Utility Bill
description: A preferred primary document used for address verification, which must be dated within the last 3 months.

name: Council Tax Document
description: A preferred primary document used for address verification.

name: Bank Statement
description: A preferred primary document used for address verification.

name: Mortgage Statement
description: A preferred primary document used for address verification.

name: Tenancy Agreement
description: A secondary document used for address verification when primary documents are unavailable.

name: Insurance Policy
description: A secondary document used for address verification when primary documents are unavailable.

name: HM Revenue & Customs Letter
description: A secondary document used for address verification when primary documents are unavailable.

name: Electoral Register Extract
description: A secondary document used for address verification when primary documents are unavailable.

name: Verification Process
description: An operational workflow focused on the collection, validation, and recording of customer address documentation to ensure residency verification.

name: Document Collection Step
description: The initial stage of the verification process where the operator requests an address verification document and records the specific document type and date.

name: Address Verification Step
description: A validation stage involving the comparison of the address on the ID against the provided address document, specifically checking for UK postcode format and consistency.
context: Compare address on ID with address document

name: System Recording Step
description: The final administrative stage where the document type is entered into the system, linked to the specific customer record, and the address status is updated to 'verified'.

name: Address Match Decision
description: A critical check within the verification step to determine if the address on the ID matches the provided address document.

name: Address Validity Compliance Checkpoint
description: A mandatory control point to ensure the address adheres to UK formatting and matches identification documents before the record is marked as verified.

name: AML Screening Step
description: A discrete stage in the operational workflow dedicated to Anti-Money Laundering screening. The execution of this step is governed by the detailed procedures outlined in the policy_aml document.

name: Sanctions and PEP Screening Process
description: The operational workflow for screening customers against global sanctions lists and Politically Exposed Person (PEP) databases. It defines both mandatory screening requirements for all customers and additional requirements for those identified as high-risk.

name: OFAC Sanctions Check
description: A mandatory regulatory gate where the customer is screened against the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Sanctions List.
context: Mandatory Screening Against: OFAC Sanctions List

name: EU Consolidated Sanctions Check
description: A mandatory regulatory gate where the customer is screened against the EU Consolidated Sanctions List.
context: Mandatory Screening Against: EU Consolidated Sanctions List

name: HMT Sanctions Check
description: A mandatory regulatory gate where the customer is screened against the HM Treasury (HMT) Sanctions List.
context: Mandatory Screening Against: HMT Sanctions List

name: UN Sanctions Check
description: A mandatory regulatory gate where the customer is screened against the United Nations (UN) Sanctions List.
context: Mandatory Screening Against: UN Sanctions List

name: PEP Database Screening
description: A mandatory regulatory gate to identify if a customer is a Politically Exposed Person (PEP) via database screening.

name: Adverse Media Screening
description: An additional compliance gate required specifically for customers classified as high-risk to identify negative news or reputational risk.

name: Beneficial Ownership Verification
description: An additional compliance gate for high-risk entities to verify the identity of the beneficial owners.

name: Risk Level Determination
description: A branching point in the screening process that determines if a customer is 'Standard' (requiring only mandatory screening) or 'High-Risk' (requiring additional adverse media and beneficial ownership checks).

name: Screening Process
description: An operational workflow used to screen customers against sanctions, PEP, and adverse media lists. The process is primarily automated with manual review for matches, typically completing within 5–10 minutes.
context: Processing Time: 5–10 minutes (automated with manual review if needed)

name: Name Screening Step
description: The initial phase where the customer name is automatically checked against all relevant lists. Results are generated by the system in less than one minute.
context: Customer name screened against all lists

name: Match Assessment Step
description: The stage where screening results are evaluated to determine if a match is a true hit or a false positive based on name similarity. If a match is found, it triggers a manual review by the Compliance team.
context: False positive assessment (name similarity vs. true match)
If match found: Manual review by Compliance

name: Hit Handling Step
description: The action phase following a confirmed match, where different handling paths are taken based on whether the hit is a sanctions match, a PEP match, or adverse media.
context: If sanctions match: Escalate immediately, account blocked, Compliance notified
If PEP match: Enhanced due diligence required
If adverse media: Risk assessment, possible rejection

name: Screening Record Entry Step
description: The final step where screening results, identified matches, and their resolutions are documented in the system and linked to the customer's account record.

name: Compliance Team
description: The personnel responsible for performing manual reviews of screening matches and receiving notifications regarding sanctions hits.

name: Screening System
description: The automated engine that performs name screening against lists and generates results within one minute.

name: Match Found Decision
description: A branching point after name screening to determine if a match was found. No match leads to the next step, while a match triggers a manual compliance review.
context: If no match: Proceed to next step
If match found: Manual review by Compliance

name: Hit Type Classification Decision
description: A decision point that routes the process based on the type of match: sanctions (immediate escalation/block), PEP (enhanced due diligence), or adverse media (risk assessment/rejection).
context: If PEP match: Enhanced due diligence required
If adverse media: Risk assessment, possible rejection

name: Sanctions and PEP Screening Checkpoint
description: A mandatory compliance gate verifying that the customer has been screened against sanctions and PEP lists before the account can proceed.
context: Customer name screened against all lists
If sanctions match: Escalate immediately, account blocked

name: Screened Customer
description: The individual whose name is being screened against regulatory and risk lists.
context: Customer name screened against all lists

name: Screened Account
description: The customer account associated with the screening process, which may be blocked in the event of a sanctions match.

name: Risk Assessment Step
description: A discrete stage in the onboarding process where the customer's risk level is determined based on demographic, residency, and status criteria. This step involves assigning a risk category based on specific risk scoring factors.

name: Customer Risk Level Determination
description: A branching decision point where a customer is categorized as Low, Medium, or High risk based on age, nationality, PEP status, adverse media, and account size. The outcome determines the final risk category assigned to the customer.

name: PEP Status Check
description: A mandatory compliance check to determine if a customer is a Politically Exposed Person (PEP) or a member of a PEP family. A 'yes' outcome triggers a higher risk classification.

name: Adverse Media Screening
description: A compliance verification step to check for adverse media associated with the customer. The presence of adverse media results in a higher risk assignment.

name: Risk-Assessed Customer
description: The individual undergoing risk scoring during the assessment process. Their attributes such as age, nationality, and status are used to determine their risk category.

name: Risk-Rated Banking Product
description: The specific banking product or account size being applied for, which influences the overall risk score (e.g., standard vs high-value).
context: Standard customer, standard product, standard amount

name: Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) Process
description: A specialized due diligence procedure triggered when a customer is identified as high-risk. It involves senior staff review, ownership verification, fund documentation, and final approval by the Compliance Head.

name: Senior Staff Review Step
description: The initial step in the EDD process where senior staff members conduct a review of the high-risk profile.

name: Beneficial Ownership Verification Step
description: A verification process to identify and confirm the beneficial owners when the customer is an entity.

name: Source of Funds Documentation Step
description: The collection and verification of documentation proving the origin of the customer's funds.

name: Additional Screening Step
description: Supplemental screening measures performed as part of the enhanced due diligence requirements.

name: Compliance Head Approval Step
description: The final step in the EDD workflow requiring formal sign-off from the Compliance Head.

name: Senior Staff
description: Personnel responsible for performing the initial review of high-risk customers during the EDD process.

name: Compliance Head
description: The ultimate authority responsible for approving the EDD process and acting as the escalation point.
context: Refer to Compliance Head for approval

name: High-Risk Trigger Gate
description: A decision point that determines if the standard process should be escalated to the Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) workflow based on the customer's risk level.

name: Compliance Head Escalation Level
description: The highest tier of escalation for EDD, where the Compliance Head provides final approval for high-risk cases.
context: EDD Escalation: Refer to Compliance Head for approval

name: EDD Compliance Approval Checkpoint
description: The mandatory regulatory gate where the Compliance Head verifies all EDD steps have been completed and grants formal approval.
context: Refer to Compliance Head for approval

name: Account Opening Process
description: The end-to-end procedure for opening a bank account, including the final approval/rejection phase based on KYC, address, and AML criteria. Approval timelines vary by channel: immediate for branch, under one hour for online, and 1-2 business days for postal.
context: Account opening form complete and accurate

name: Approval/Rejection Decision Step
description: The final stage of the account opening process where the application is evaluated against specific approval criteria to determine if the account can be opened.

name: Account Approval Gate
description: A decision point where an account is approved if KYC, address verification, AML screening, risk assessment, and form accuracy are all successful. Failure to meet these criteria leads to rejection.

name: Account Manager
description: The actor responsible for providing approval for accounts classified as Low-Medium Risk.

name: Compliance Head
description: The actor responsible for providing approval for accounts classified as High Risk.

name: Chief Risk Officer (CRO)
description: The high-level authority responsible for approving accounts that require a policy exception.

name: KYC Completion Checkpoint
description: A mandatory regulatory gate verifying that KYC verification is complete and successful before account approval.

name: Address Verification Checkpoint
description: A mandatory control point verifying that the customer's address has been successfully verified.

name: AML and Sanctions Checkpoint
description: A regulatory gate verifying that AML screening has passed and no sanctions hits were identified.

name: Risk Assessment Checkpoint
description: A policy gate verifying that the risk assessment for the applicant is within acceptable parameters.

name: Account Rejection Process
description: The operational workflow for rejecting a customer's account application based on failed KYC, AML, PEP, or regulatory checks. It defines the triggers for rejection and the mandatory notification protocol to prevent tipping off.

name: Account Application Approval Gate
description: A critical branching point where the application is rejected if any of the listed KYC, AML, PEP, beneficial ownership, source of funds, or regulatory criteria are not met.

name: KYC Identity Verification Checkpoint
description: A mandatory compliance gate to verify the identity of the applicant. Failure to verify identity results in immediate account rejection.

name: AML Sanctions Screening Checkpoint
description: A compliance gate to check for sanctions matches. A confirmed sanctions match triggers an account rejection.

name: PEP and Adverse Media Risk Checkpoint
description: A regulatory check for Politically Exposed Persons or adverse media. The account is rejected if the associated risk cannot be mitigated.

name: Beneficial Ownership Verification Checkpoint
description: A mandatory check for entity customers to ensure clear beneficial ownership. Unclear ownership leads to account rejection.

name: Source of Funds Fraud Checkpoint
description: A verification step to assess the legitimacy of the customer's source of funds. Suspicious findings trigger a rejection due to fraud concerns.

name: Regulatory Exception Approval Checkpoint
description: A final gate to determine if a regulatory exception has been granted. If the exception is denied, the account is rejected.

name: Rejection Notification Issuance
description: The act of sending a written notice to the customer stating the account cannot be opened. To prevent 'tipping off', no specific AML reasons or detailed explanations are provided.
context: Written notice to customer (no AML reason disclosed—tipping off risk)
Letter: "We are unable to open your account at this time. Please contact us for more information."

name: Customer
description: The individual or entity applying for an account who is the subject of the KYC/AML checks and the recipient of the rejection notice.

name: Account Creation Process
description: The operational workflow for creating a new bank account through Branch or Online channels. It involves system setup in AMS and configuration of product settings with an automated processing time of less than 15 minutes.

name: AMS Account Creation
description: The initial action of creating the account record within the Account Management System (AMS).
context: Account created in AMS (Account Management System)

name: Account Number Assignment
description: The process of assigning a unique account identifier following the format ACC-00XXX.

name: Product Settings Configuration
description: The configuration of specific product parameters associated with the new account.

name: Interest Rate Setup
description: The application of the interest rate to the account based on the current applicable schedule.

name: Linked System Update
description: The synchronization of the new account details across integrated platforms, specifically including online banking and the fraud engine.
context: Linked systems updated (online banking, fraud engine, etc.)

name: AMS (Account Management System)
description: The primary system used for creating and recording account details during the opening process.
context: Account created in AMS (Account Management System)

name: Fraud Engine
description: A linked system that must be updated during the account creation process to enable fraud monitoring.
context: Linked systems updated (online banking, fraud engine, etc.)

name: New Account
description: The customer account being established in the AMS, assigned a number, and configured with product settings.

name: Initial Balance Funding Process
description: The procedure for establishing the initial balance of a new account, providing various deposit options including cash, transfers, and zero-balance setups. The process concludes with the account being set to 'Active' status.

name: Cash Deposit Processing
description: A funding step performed at a physical branch location. Deposits are capped at a maximum of £10k per individual transaction.
context: Cash Deposit: At branch (max £10k per transaction)

name: FPS Transfer Processing
description: A funding step where funds are moved from an existing bank account using the Faster Payments System (FPS).

name: Mobile Check Deposit
description: A proposed funding method via the mobile application, currently noted as a future feature.
context: Check Deposit: Via mobile app (future feature)

name: Zero Balance Account Setup
description: An option allowing the account to be created without any initial funding, resulting in a £0 balance.
context: No Initial Deposit: Account created with £0 balance

name: Branch Staff
description: The personnel responsible for facilitating and accepting cash deposits at the branch location.

name: New Account
description: The bank account being funded and activated through the Initial Balance process.

name: Card Issuance Process
description: The operational workflow for issuing and activating debit cards for customers, covering branch, online, and postal channels. The process includes card ordering, delivery timelines, and PIN setup procedures.
context: Card issued immediately (if available in branch)
Card ordered via mail (5–7 business days)

name: Card Issuance Execution
description: The action of providing a Visa Debit card to the customer. Delivery method and timing vary by channel: immediate for branch, and 5–7 business days for online or postal orders.
context: Branch: Card issued immediately (if available in branch)
Online: Card ordered via mail (5–7 business days)
Postal: Card ordered after account approved (5–7 days)

name: PIN Setup Procedure
description: The process of establishing a Personal Identification Number for the issued card. Methods vary by channel, utilizing PinPads in-branch or online/phone options for remote customers.
context: Branch: PIN set by customer at branch (PinPad)
Online: PIN set online or via phone
Postal: PIN set via phone or online

name: Customer
description: The account holder who receives the card and is responsible for setting their own PIN via the provided channel methods.
context: PIN set by customer at branch (PinPad)

name: Visa Debit Card
description: The specific banking product issued, characterized as a Visa Debit card with contactless and chip capabilities and a 3-year validity period.

name: Debit Card Activation
description: The status transition of the issued Visa Debit card from inactive to active through the completion of the PIN setup process.
context: PIN set by customer at branch (PinPad)

name: Card Activation Procedure
description: The end-to-end workflow for activating a payment card received by a customer. The process is completed same day if performed at a branch or by the next business day if performed online.
context: Card Activation Time: Same day (if at branch), next business day (if online)

name: Card Delivery Step
description: The initial stage where the customer receives the physical payment card via mail.

name: Activation Channel Selection
description: The step where the customer initiates activation through one of three approved channels: online, mobile, or phone.

name: PIN Confirmation Step
description: The verification stage where the card's Personal Identification Number (PIN) is confirmed.

name: Card Transactional Activation
description: The final state where the card is officially active and available for use in transactions.

name: Customer
description: The bank customer who receives the card and performs the activation steps via the specified channels.

name: Payment Card
description: The physical payment card that is sent to the customer and must be activated before it can be used for transactions.

name: Account Opening Process
description: The end-to-end procedure for opening a new bank account, encompassing various customer channels including Branch, Online, and Postal. The process culminates in customer notification and the provision of account details.

name: Customer Notification Step
description: The final stage of the account opening process where the customer is informed that their account has been successfully created. The method of notification varies based on the channel used by the customer.

name: Branch Staff
description: The personnel responsible for providing verbal and written confirmation and distributing welcome packs to customers visiting the branch.
context: Branch Customers: Verbal confirmation at branch

name: Automated Notification System
description: The system responsible for triggering immediate email confirmations and welcome emails to customers who apply online.

name: Branch Customer
description: A customer who opens an account via a physical branch and receives immediate verbal and written confirmation.
context: Branch Customers: Verbal confirmation at branch

name: Online Customer
description: A customer who opens an account via digital channels and receives immediate email notifications.
context: Online Customers: Email confirmation (immediate after account creation)

name: Postal Customer
description: A customer who opens an account via post and receives confirmation via a letter sent the following day.
context: Postal Customers: Letter confirmation (posted next day)

name: New Account
description: The account being created for the customer, for which the account number, sort code, and login details are generated and shared.
context: Account number, sort code, online login details
Includes account number, sort code, online login setup instructions

name: Welcome Communications Process
description: The operational workflow for delivering introductory materials to new customers, including CEO letters, product guides, and fraud advice. Delivery timelines vary by channel: same day for branch, next day for email, and 2–3 days for postal delivery.
context: Delivery: Same day (branch), next day (email), 2–3 days (postal)

name: Welcome Letter Issuance
description: The action of providing a formal welcome letter from the CEO to the customer as part of the communication package.

name: Product Guide Distribution
description: The delivery of the product guide containing terms, features, and FAQs to the customer.

name: Getting Started Guide Distribution
description: The delivery of instructions regarding online banking and the mobile app to help the customer begin using bank services.
context: Getting started guide (online banking, mobile app)

name: Contact Information Provision
description: The provision of bank contact details to the customer within the welcome package.

name: Fraud Prevention Advice Delivery
description: The delivery of guidance to the customer on how to prevent fraud.

name: Account Activation Process
description: The end-to-end procedure for activating a customer's account through both Online Banking and Mobile App setup. It involves credential delivery, security configuration, and biometric enrollment to enable transactions.

name: Credential Delivery
description: The initial stage of online banking setup where the customer is provided with their login credentials.

name: Online Banking Portal Access
description: The action where the customer navigates to the official FirstUK Bank login URL to begin the activation process.

name: Password Permanency Update
description: The security step where the customer replaces their temporary password with a permanent one.

name: Security Question Configuration
description: The setup of security questions to ensure account protection and verification.

name: Online Banking Activation Completion
description: The final state where the online banking facility is fully enabled for the customer.

name: Mobile Application Installation
description: The step where the customer downloads the official FirstUK Bank application to their device.

name: Mobile App Authentication
description: The process of logging into the mobile application using the previously established online banking credentials.

name: Biometric Security Setup
description: The configuration of biometric identifiers, such as fingerprint or face ID, for secure app access.

name: Mobile App Transaction Activation
description: The final stage where the mobile application is fully enabled for performing financial transactions.

name: Customer
description: The primary actor responsible for performing the activation steps, including password resets and biometric setup.

name: Access Activation Process
description: The end-to-end operational workflow to transition an account to a fully active state. It encompasses KYC, AML, system creation, card issuance, and customer notification, with a completion timeline of 1–7 business days.

name: KYC Verification Step
description: The stage where Know Your Customer verification is performed and completed to enable account activation.

name: AML Screening Step
description: The process of screening the account holder against Anti-Money Laundering lists to ensure a passing result.

name: System Account Creation
description: The administrative action of creating the account records across all required bank systems.

name: Card Issuance and Activation
description: The step involving the physical or digital issuance and subsequent activation of a payment card, if applicable to the account type.

name: Digital Access Configuration
description: The technical setup of online and mobile banking access for the customer.

name: Customer Notification Step
description: The final action of notifying the customer that their account is fully active and ready for use.

name: KYC Compliance Checkpoint
description: A mandatory regulatory gate verifying that the KYC process has been successfully completed before the account can be marked as active.

name: AML Compliance Checkpoint
description: A mandatory regulatory gate verifying that the AML screening has passed before the account can be marked as active.

name: Customer
description: The subject of the activation process who must be notified once all activation criteria are met.

name: Account Quality Assurance Process
description: A comprehensive quality assurance and error-checking workflow conducted both before and after account approval to ensure data accuracy, compliance adherence, and correct system setup.

name: Pre-Approval Compliance and Data Validation
description: A critical review stage occurring before account approval to verify that all fields are complete, KYC and AML checks are passed, and risk assessments are documented.

name: Post-Approval System and Notification Execution
description: The final stage of the process following approval, focusing on account creation in the system, updating linked systems, ordering cards, and notifying the customer.

name: KYC Verification Checkpoint
description: A mandatory control gate ensuring that identity and address verification have been completed before the account can proceed to approval.

name: AML Screening Checkpoint
description: A regulatory gate requiring confirmation that the AML screening process has been successfully passed prior to account approval.

name: Authority-Based Approval Gate
description: A decision point where approval must be obtained based on the specific authority limits of the reviewer before the process can move to the post-approval stage.

name: Approving Authority
description: The individual or role with the designated authority to provide final approval for the account opening based on the completed QA checks.

name: Risk Assessment Documentation
description: The step of documenting the risk assessment associated with the account as part of the pre-approval quality check.

name: Card Ordering Process
description: An optional post-approval step where a payment card is ordered if applicable to the specific account product.

name: Monthly Audit Process
description: A recurring monthly procedure to sample account opening files to ensure compliance with KYC/AML standards, data accuracy, and timeliness. The process aims for an error rate of less than 0.5%.

name: Account Opening File Review
description: The initial stage of the monthly audit where a sample of 10 or more account opening files are selected and reviewed for compliance.

name: KYC and AML Completion Verification
description: A mandatory control point within the audit to verify that all required Know Your Customer (KYC) and Anti-Money Laundering (AML) procedures were completed for the sampled accounts.

name: Data Accuracy Verification
description: An audit step focused on ensuring that the data entered into the systems matches the supporting documentation in the account opening file.

name: Timeliness Assessment
description: An evaluation of whether the account opening process was completed within the bank's defined expected timeframes.

name: Error Rate Threshold Check
description: A decision gate to determine if the monthly audit results meet the quality standard, requiring an error rate of less than 0.5% to be considered successful.

name: Common Issues and Resolution Process
description: A workflow for identifying and resolving common discrepancies and system issues encountered during the onboarding or account maintenance phase, including KYC, address, and AML failures.

name: Expired KYC Document Resolution
description: The action of requesting a new, valid identity document from the customer when the submitted ID has expired.

name: Address Mismatch Resolution
description: The process of explaining address requirements to the customer and requesting current address verification when ID and verification addresses do not match.
context: Explain requirement, request current address verification

name: AML Screening Delay Management
description: Handling delays in AML screening caused by system lags or hits, involving waiting for confirmation and escalating if the delay persists.
context: Wait for confirmation, escalate if needed

name: Incomplete Form Resolution
description: Contacting the customer to request missing information when application fields have been left blank.

name: Online Opening System Issue Resolution
description: Handling slow system processing during online account opening by retrying the process or contacting support if the issue is persistent.

name: AML Delay Escalation Gate
description: A decision point during an AML screening delay to determine if the wait time has exceeded thresholds requiring escalation.
context: Wait for confirmation, escalate if needed

name: Customer
description: The individual providing identity documents, completing forms, and verifying address details.

name: Support Team
description: The internal support entity contacted to resolve persistent system processing issues during online account opening.

name: KYC Document Validity Check
description: A mandatory control point to verify that the provided identification document is current and not expired.

name: Address Consistency Check
description: A compliance gate ensuring that the address on the ID matches the verification address provided by the customer.

name: AML Screening Gate
description: A regulatory control point requiring confirmation of AML screening status before proceeding with the application.

name: Staff Training and Competency Process
description: The end-to-end procedure for ensuring bank staff are trained and certified in operational procedures, including annual refreshers and practical assessments.

name: Annual Training Completion
description: The requirement for staff to undergo annual training across account opening, KYC, AML, and compliance obligations, as well as product-specific system training.

name: Knowledge Assessment
description: A formal certification step where staff must pass a knowledge assessment to demonstrate theoretical understanding of procedures.

name: Observed Practice Review
description: A practical certification step where a manager observes the staff member performing operational tasks to ensure competency.

name: Senior Staff Shadowing
description: A practical training requirement where staff must shadow senior personnel for a minimum of 10 account processes.

name: Bank Staff
description: The personnel responsible for completing annual training, passing assessments, and undergoing observed practice.

name: Manager
description: The actor responsible for conducting the observed practice assessment of staff members.

name: Senior Staff
description: Experienced personnel who provide shadowing opportunities for staff during the certification process.

name: Head of Retail Banking
description: The executive role responsible for authoring and updating the SOP, including the addition of online opening procedures, card activation, and updated KYC requirements.

name: Head of Retail Banking
description: Senior executive responsible for the operational approval and sign-off of the banking procedure document.
context: Approved by: Head of Retail Banking

name: Head of Compliance
description: Senior executive responsible for ensuring the procedure meets regulatory requirements and providing formal sign-off.

name: Chief Operating Officer
description: Top-level executive providing final operational approval and sign-off for the document.
